title: Command Injection in Kernel#open and System Backticks
platform_conditions: Ruby 3.x standard library; MRI on POSIX (Kernel#open and IO.read detect a leading pipe character regardless of intent)
security_mechanism: Kernel#open and IO.read treat a string beginning with '|' as a command line and spawn it through the shell, so a filename parameter that an attacker prefixes with '| ' becomes command execution without any shell API appearing in the code. system, exec, backticks, %x and IO.popen/Open3 invoked with a single interpolated string likewise pass the whole text to /bin/sh, letting ; | $() split or append commands. File.open and FileUtils do not perform the pipe check, so the sink choice — Kernel#open versus File.open — decides exploitability.

source_sink_clues.source: Request-derived file names, command fragments and arguments reaching these APIs directly or through interpolation.
source_sink_clues.sink: Kernel#open(attacker_string); IO.read(attacker_string); system / exec / backticks / %x; IO.popen and Open3 calls with a single shell string

tracking_guards: Require array-form IO.popen/Open3 with a fixed argv[0]; require File.open/FileUtils (no pipe processing) for genuine file access; require input validation that rejects a leading '|' and shell metacharacters before any string form is used.
not_candidate_when: File access goes through File.open/FileUtils which never spawn shells, command arguments are passed as array elements with a constant executable, or the value is validated to contain no leading pipe and no shell metacharacters before use.
public_references: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/78.html
